chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging in laryngopharyngeal cancer is critical for treatment planning but remains challenging due to complex tumor invasion patterns. Current CT-based staging is subjective and labor-intensive, while biopsy is invasive. Existing computational methods either ignore anatomical structure or rely on labor-intensive tumor segmentation. Radiology reports contain organ-specific invasion details, but current multimodal models use global fusion, failing to align specific anatomical structures with their textual descriptions. This work addresses these gaps by proposing an anatomy-aware, fine-grained multimodal framework that integrates CT and radiology reports without requiring manual tumor masks.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem, including the challenges of CT-based staging and limitations of existing methods, matching the reference.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: We propose a three-module framework: 1) Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) constructs an organ-level graph using pre-trained organ segmentations and clinical prior knowledge to model invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs. 2) Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) performs fine-grained alignment by using each organ node as a query over the radiology report to selectively aggregate relevant textual evidence, enhancing organ features while preserving anatomical topology. 3) Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG) uses a large language model to extract explicit invasion statements from the report and injects them as a text node connected only to primary sites and invaded organs, refining the graph without discarding anatomy-based risk connections.
chk_method.reason: The poster provides a detailed description of the proposed framework and its components, consistent with the reference.

In binary classification (T1-T2 vs T3-T4), our method achieved 80.83% F1 and 81.53% accuracy internally, and 76.46% F1 and 76.50% accuracy externally, outperforming the best baseline (MMI) by 3.24% F1 internally and 2.37% F1 externally. chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduced an anatomy-structured multimodal framework for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging that integrates CT and radiology reports via AOG, OCA, and REG modules. It captures organ-specific invasion patterns and textual evidence, achieving state-of-the-art performance and matching radiologist accuracy. The framework offers improved interpretability by aligning decisions with clinically meaningful invasion pathways.
